summary:
Targets-only review of stage 2 (C2, C3) at head 48a34b0. One target per clause; a test is named for each, and test gaps are marked EXPECTED SURVIVOR. Main weakness: in --style auto, when no References line parses as an [N] entry, the checker falls back to APA and silently drops every numeric citation, then exits 0. CJK narrative citations and non-ASCII surnames are also invisible.

Mutation targets (selected by adversary):
1. C2/APA citation-without-entry: integrity_gate.py:152 apa_citations, drop the `re.split(r"\s*[;；]\s*", ...)` so each parenthetical group is one part. Should fail: test_apa_in_text_citation_without_entry_fails (novak, 2020 no longer named).
2. C2/APA et-al form: integrity_gate.py:107 APA_PART_RE, delete the `\s+et al\.?` alternative. Should fail: test_clean_apa_proposal_passes (wang, 2022a entry never cited).
3. C2/APA entry-never-cited: integrity_gate.py:171-175 reconcile, change the second comprehension's guard `if key not in cited` to `if False`. Should fail: test_apa_entry_never_cited_fails, test_apa_year_mismatch_is_an_orphan_both_ways. It also hits research-paper test_bib_entry_never_cited_fails. A proposal-only variant: check_proposal.py:77 use `apa_entries(body)` in place of `apa_entries(refs)`.
4. C2/APA narrative: integrity_gate.py:155-156, remove the APA_NARRATIVE_RE loop. Should fail: test_apa_narrative_citation_is_reconciled, test_clean_apa_proposal_passes (okafor, 2021 never cited).
5. C2/numeric citation-without-entry (range boundary): integrity_gate.py:124 expand_numeric, change `range(bounds[0], bounds[1] + 1)` to `range(bounds[0], bounds[1])`. Should fail: test_clean_numeric_proposal_passes ([3] never cited), test_numeric_range_expands.
6. C2/numeric orphan both ways: check_proposal.py:73-75, use `numeric_entries(body)` in place of `numeric_entries(refs)`. Should fail: test_numeric_citation_without_entry_fails, test_numeric_entry_never_cited_fails.
7. C2/numeric full-width separator (EXPECTED SURVIVOR, a test gap): integrity_gate.py:100 NUMERIC_CITE_RE, remove `，` from `[-–—,，]`. No test cites `[1，3]`, so nothing fails. Add a GB/T fixture with a full-width comma.
8. C2/auto style detection: check_proposal.py:71, invert to `"apa" if numeric_entries(refs) else "numeric"`. Should fail: test_clean_numeric_proposal_passes, test_clean_apa_proposal_passes. Note: test_auto_detects_numeric_from_entries passes `--style` explicitly, so it does not exercise auto at all.
9. C2/no References section: check_proposal.py:69, change `if count else []` to `[]`. Should fail: test_citations_without_references_section_fail.
10. C2/placeholder: check_proposal.py:85, scan `""` in place of `text`, or append `$` to PLACEHOLDER_PATTERN. Should fail: test_placeholder_fails, plus test_placeholder_pattern_is_the_documented_grep for the pattern edit.
11. C2/disclosure downgrade guard (EXPECTED SURVIVOR, a test gap): check_proposal.py:87, change `allow_flags and DISCLOSED_FLAG_RE.match(hit)` to `allow_flags`, so a fake DOI or 10.xxxx becomes a WARN under --allow-disclosed-flags. No proposal test exercises that path. The paper-side analogue R3 was fixed (test_disclosure_flag_does_not_excuse_other_placeholders) but not ported here.
12. C2/AI-tell case-insensitivity: check_proposal.py:90, set `ignore_case=False`. Should fail: test_ai_tell_in_body_fails ('In recent years,'). test_chinese_ai_tell_fails guards the 中文 alternatives: delete `|近年来，?随着` together with the SKILL.md grep, and that test should fail.
13. C2/AI-tell body-only (EXPECTED SURVIVOR, a test gap): check_proposal.py:88-91, scan `text` in place of `body_text` and report `index` as the line. No test puts an AI-tell phrase in References, so nothing fails.
14. C2/scaffold-bracket detection: check_proposal.py:101-103, make the exemption test always true (`or True`). Should fail: test_leftover_scaffold_bracket_fails.
15. C2/scaffold exemptions: check_proposal.py:55-56, remove `所属学科` (or `University/Institution Name`) from EXEMPT_BRACKETS. Should fail: test_exempt_personalization_fields_are_not_flagged, test_clean_*_passes. check_proposal.py:58, remove `|图\s*\d+\s*建议`: test_clean_numeric_proposal_passes should fail. check_proposal.py:60, remove the numeric alternative from NOT_SCAFFOLD_RE: test_clean_numeric_proposal_passes should fail, because body [1] gets flagged.
16. C2/exemption anchoring (EXPECTED SURVIVOR): check_proposal.py:58, drop the `$` from EXEMPT_BRACKET_RE, so `[Figure 1 Suggestion: write caption here]` escapes. Also `\d+` to `\d`, which breaks [Figure 10 Suggestion]. No test covers either.
17. C2/exit codes: integrity_gate.py:247, `return EXIT_FINDINGS` to `return EXIT_CLEAN`. Should fail: every *_fails test (assertEqual(code, 1)). integrity_gate.py:21, EXIT_USAGE=1: test_missing_file_is_usage_error should fail. check_proposal.py:116, `is_file()` to `exists()` (EXPECTED SURVIVOR: a directory or non-UTF-8 input crashes with Python's exit 1, which reads as 'findings', not 2).
18. C3/core present in both: delete research-proposal/scripts/integrity_gate.py (as a mutant patch only). Should fail: test_every_carrier_has_the_core, plus the import error in test_check_proposal.py.
19. C3/both checkers import it: check_proposal.py:28, replace `from integrity_gate import (...)` with `import integrity_gate as _g` plus aliases, or inline the functions. Should fail: test_each_gate_imports_the_core. Weakness: that test is a text regex, so a checker that imports but then locally redefines reconcile/split_body still passes.
20. C3/byte-identical: change one byte in research-paper/scripts/integrity_gate.py only, e.g. `EXIT_USAGE = 2` to `3`, or add a trailing space or CRLF on one line. Should fail: test_copies_are_byte_identical. The proposal-copy mirror mutant should fail the same test.

findings.title: auto style silently drops all numeric citations when References entries don't parse as [N], so the gate exits 0
findings.what_goes_wrong: In auto mode (the documented default), the style is numeric only if some References line matches NUMERIC_ENTRY_RE `^\s*(?:[-*]\s*)?\[(\d+)\]`. Otherwise the checker switches to APA. On a GB/T proposal this yields zero APA citations in the body and zero APA entries in References (GB/T entries have no parenthesised year), so reconcile({}, {}) returns nothing and the gate prints 'no mechanical findings' (exit 0), even with orphan [N] citations in either direction. Inputs that trigger it: References written as a markdown ordered list (`1. 史密斯. 题名[J]...`), escaped brackets from Typora/pandoc (`\[1\] ...`), or IME full-width `［1］`. I checked the copied regexes: none of these three entry forms matches NUMERIC_ENTRY_RE or APA_ENTRY_RE.
findings.why_vulnerable: Detection failure falls back to a style that cannot see the body's citations, and the checker never cross-checks: numeric citations present in the body plus non-blank References lines plus zero parsed entries is never reported. SKILL.md now tells the agent this gate 'performs every mechanical check below in one pass', with the manual bullets demoted to fallback, so a silent pass replaces the manual reconciliation. Inference: the agent will not run the manual check after exit 0.
findings.how_to_confirm: Take NUMERIC_CLEAN from research-proposal/tests/test_check_proposal.py, rewrite the References lines as `1. 史密斯...`, `2. ...` and change one body citation to [9]. Run check_proposal.main([path]): expect exit 0 and no FAIL lines. Repeat with `\[1\]`-escaped entries.
findings.recommendation: In check_citations: when the body has numeric citations but style resolves to APA (or the References section has non-blank, non-comment lines but zero parsed entries), emit a FAIL such as 'unparsed-references' giving the count of unparsed lines. Accept `\[N\]`, `N.` and `［N］` entries. Add a test with an ordered-list References section and an orphan [9].

findings.title: Chinese narrative citations are invisible, and the `等` narrative form is keyed wrong (CJK \w lookbehind, same bug class as R1)
findings.what_goes_wrong: APA_NARRATIVE_RE starts with `(?<![\w(])`. Python's \w matches CJK, so `研究表明张伟（2020）提出` produces no match at any start position: the citation is ignored, and if it has no References entry nothing is reported. When `张伟等（2020）` follows punctuation it does match, but greedy `[一-鿿]{1,4}` captures `张伟等` and narrative has no `等` handling, so the key is '张伟等, 2020' against the entry key '张伟, 2020'. The result is a false citation-without-entry plus entry-never-cited. Confirmed with the regex copied into python3 -I -c.
findings.why_vulnerable: The fix for R1 (ASCII-only boundaries for metric numbers) was not applied to the citation regexes, and no test uses Chinese author-year citations. Both fixtures are English APA and Chinese GB/T.
findings.how_to_confirm: Add a Chinese APA fixture whose body has `已有研究表明张伟（2020）提出…`, with References missing 张伟 2020: expect exit 0 (silent miss). A second fixture with `，张伟等（2020）` and entry `张伟, 李明. (2020)...`: expect two spurious FAILs.
findings.recommendation: Use an ASCII-only lookbehind, e.g. `(?<![A-Za-z0-9_(])`, for the Latin alternative. For CJK, anchor on preceding punctuation or else accept the 2-3 chars directly before （. Handle `等` and `和/、` in APA_NARRATIVE_RE as APA_PART_RE already does. Add a Chinese APA fixture covering clean, orphan-citation and orphan-entry cases.

findings.title: Non-ASCII surnames and common APA variants are skipped in both directions
findings.what_goes_wrong: _SURNAME `[A-Z][A-Za-z'’\-]+` rejects Müller, Çelik, Østergaard, Šimić and similar. `(Müller, 2020)` is not parsed as a citation, and `Müller, K. (2020)...` is not parsed as an entry. An uncited Müller entry is never flagged, and a Müller citation with no entry is never flagged. Likewise `(Smith et al. 2024)` (no comma) and `(Smith, 2020, 2022)` (multiple years) fail APA_PART_RE and are dropped. The dropped multi-year case is a silent false negative for a missing 2022 entry. Verified with copied regexes.
findings.why_vulnerable: Anything a regex does not match is silently skipped rather than reported as unparsed, so coverage gaps look like clean passes.
findings.how_to_confirm: Append `Müller, K. (2020). Unused. *Venue*.` to APA_CLEAN: expect exit 0, although C2 requires entry-never-cited.
findings.recommendation: Use `[^\W\d_]` (Unicode letters) with an uppercase check, or `\w`-based classes with a Unicode-aware first letter. Allow an optional comma before the year, and split `Smith, 2020, 2022` into one key per year. Also report References lines in the References section that match neither entry regex as WARN or FAIL.

findings.title: Scaffold instructions under References, including the scaffold's own word-count footer, escape the scaffold-bracket check; subheadings inside References drop entries
findings.what_goes_wrong: check_scaffold_brackets scans only `body`. In both shipped scaffolds the References section contains bracketed instructions (`[遵循相应的引用格式：GB/T 7714、APA或其他]`, `[Follow appropriate citation style: APA, MLA, or Chicago]`, `[Include a mix of foundational works...]`). The footer `*总字数：[研究计划约5,000字…]*` / `*Total Word Count: [~3,000 words excluding references]*` also sits after `## References` with no heading in between. A draft that keeps any of these passes. Separately, split_body (integrity_gate.py:60) leaves the References section at any non-References heading, so `### 中文文献` / `### 外文文献` subgroups, which are common in 开题报告, move their entries into the body. Those entries are then neither listed nor cited, and an uncited entry in such a group is never flagged.
findings.why_vulnerable: The References section is excluded from the scaffold scan to avoid GB/T `[J]`/`[M]` type markers, but nothing else checks it for scaffold leftovers. Sub-headings are treated like section breaks.
findings.how_to_confirm: Append `[Ensure balance across different research groups and institutions]` and `*Total Word Count: [~3,000 words excluding references]*` under References in APA_CLEAN: expect exit 0. Insert `### 外文文献` before an uncited extra entry: expect no entry-never-cited.
findings.recommendation: Scan the References section for brackets too, exempting `[J]/[M]/[C]/[D]/[N]/[EB/OL]…` type codes, `[N]` entry numbers and `[C]//`. Keep in_refs across deeper sub-headings: leave it only on a heading of the same or higher level than the References heading. Add tests for both cases.

limits: snapshot-only; no command reproduction; no OS sandbox; reviewer: claude subagent (same model family as author). Regex behavior was checked by copying the regexes into standalone python3 -I -c snippets; project code and tests were not run, so survivor and kill predictions are inferred from reading the tests. evidence/MANIFEST hashes were not verified, because no evidence file is cited in these findings.
